preamble: The rhotic becomes the alveolar nasal [n] either by nasal assimilation (Ho-Chunk /r/ after a nasal vowel) or by word-final change of *-r to -n (western Old Chinese dialects, per Baxter and Sagart).
phoneticEffects: Nasalization, Change in Manner of Articulation

examples.note: /r/ is pronounced [n] when it immediately follows a nasal vowel.
Baxter and Sagart argue that final *-r became *-n in western Old Chinese dialects (and *-j in eastern ones); Zhengzhang reconstructs *sreːn.

sources: Baxter, W. H., & Sagart, L. (2014). Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction. Oxford University Press. https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199945375.001.0001
